newsitem.title: FINLAND: Forestry pick-up bolsters Helsinki bourse.
newsitem.headline: Forestry pick-up bolsters Helsinki bourse.

text.p: Shares ended slightly higher on Tuesday as forestries corrected Monday's sharp losses together with their Swedish rivals, brokers said.
The general HEX index rose 0.24 percent to 2,769.33 points as advancers beat decliners 56 yo 39. 23 issues were unchanged.

Trade was a healthy 606 million markka although telecoms major Nokia, which normally accounts for almost half of trade, was exceptionally sluggish at some 120 million markka. It fell 2.00 markka to close at 321.00.
Sentiment was cautious due to uncertainty about U.S. monetary policy caused by the start of the Federal reserve's policy setting meeting, though no rate hike was expected.
"We had a surprisingly strong session", one broker said, referring to the U.S. central bank meeting due to start later.
"We are likely to have a subdued day tomorrow," he added.

The forestry sub-index rose 1.3 percent after falling 1.1 percent on Monday, as UPM-Kymmene advanced 1.70 to 95.70 in hefty almost 120 million markka trade. Metsa-Serla B rose 0.40 to 35.90 but Enso closed flat at 39.00 markka.
Cultor rose 12.00 markka or almost five percent to 258.00 in lively dealings after it announced that its third tertial last year was its strongest and upped its full-1996 EPS estimate.
Konecranes was lively ahead of its 1996 result announcement due on Wednesday morning, up 7.00 to 162.00.
